item.title: How An 81-Year-Old Gringa launched a Mexican opera company
item.description: Kate Burt was still learning Spanish when she became involved with theater in Guanajuato. Before long, she had founded the city's first opera company. The post How An 81-Year-Old Gringa launched a Mexican opera company appeared first on Mexico News Daily

item.title: A last-minute surge in exports saved Mexico from recession in 2025
item.description: In a year marked by U.S. trade aggression, the record-breaking performance of its exports kept the Mexican economy afloat, pushing GDP growth up to a mediocre 0.7%. The post A last-minute surge in exports saved Mexico from recession in 2025 appeared first on Mexico News Daily

item.title: Maya Train tickets go on sale in Europe
item.description: By bringing ticket sales out of the country for the first time, Mexico is making it easier for Europeans to plan and pay for their visit to Mexico, including transport through the southern tourist meccas. The post Maya Train tickets go on sale in Europe appeared first on Mexico News Daily

item.title: Government deploys 1,600 troops to Sinaloa following attack on legislators
item.description: The influx of troops into the troubled state is in response to the attempted murder this week of two state congressmembers and the nearby kidnapping of 10 mine workers. The post Government deploys 1,600 troops to Sinaloa following attack on legislators appeared first on Mexico News Daily

item.title: Looting report leads to discovery of millennium-old Zapotec burial chamber
item.description: Culture Minister Cluadia Curiel called it "one of the most important findings of Zapotec culture due to its state of preservation" and said the site should be open to the public by the end of this year. item.title: Tourism Ministry, seeking to reactivate local tourism, opens new beach access points in Tulum
item.description: Tulum, traditionally been one of Mexico's favorite tourism attractions, has seen a decrease in visitors lately. Some say the privatization of public beaches is partly to blame. item.title: The last days of Ángela Peralta, the ‘Mexican Nightingale’
item.description: Ángela Peralta, the "Mexican Nightingale," went to Mazatlán in 1883 to perform, but before she could do so died in a yellow fever epidemic that gripped the city. The post The last days of Ángela Peralta, the ‘Mexican Nightingale’ appeared first on Mexico News Daily
